rain_total_mm.notes: 10-year reference baseline. MERRA-2 and IMERG kept separate. 2026 IMERG has 47 trailing missing days (16 in July-Sept window) and is treated as incomplete without zero imputation.

dry_spell_max_days.notes: Evaluated strictly on the July 1 to September 30 dry-spell window. Longest dry spell averages 3-4 days in MERRA-2 and 5-6 days in IMERG.

dry_spells_ge7d.data_type: Count of dry spells lasting >= 7 consecutive days
dry_spells_ge7d.notes: Rare in MERRA-2 (0 occurrences across 10 years); IMERG identifies 0 to 2 occurrences per season.

ndvi_cover_nov_jun.notes: Landscape vegetation-cover context only. Pixel is ~6.25 ha and reflects area tree/brush cover; do not interpret as direct single-field crop stress or yield.

slope_pct.notes: Represents area-level slope context. Very gentle plain slope (<1%) with elevation 25-26 m; low water runoff erosion risk.

soil_texture.notes: Modelled soil prediction, not laboratory test. Silt fraction not extracted; partial textural indication only.

soc.notes: Soil organic carbon: 10.1 g/kg (0-5cm), 8.1 g/kg (5-15cm), 5.5 g/kg (15-30cm). Moderately low organic matter typical of West African upland soils.

ph.notes: Moderately acidic topsoil (pH 5.2 - 5.4). Well-suited to groundnut, cowpea, and pearl millet; slightly acidic for sensitive maize varieties.

soil_moisture_regional.notes: Regional subsoil moisture snapshot (0-100cm). Nearest grid cell centroid is 6.168 km from field. Mid-month snapshots, not continuous field sensor probes.

evaluated_constraints.name: Water Source Feasibility
evaluated_constraints.details: Proposed sequences fit rain-fed rainy season window (June-October).

evaluated_constraints.name: Seed Access Feasibility
evaluated_constraints.details: Candidate crops align with Medium / Local market seed channels.

evaluated_constraints.name: Crop History Rotation Balance
evaluated_constraints.details: Past sequence maintained a balanced cereal-legume rotation.

strategies.name: Option A: Legume-Cereal Nitrogen Restoring Rotation
strategies.why: Optimizes soil fertility and disease disruption. Introducing dual-purpose cowpea in Season 1 breaks groundnut-specific leaf spot pathogens while fixing 35-50 kg N/ha for subsequent Souna millet. Year 3 pairs groundnut with drought-tolerant sesame for diversified cash income.

evidence.observation: Topsoil organic carbon is 7.9 g/kg. Incorporating leafy cowpea residue directly addresses organic matter deficit.
Short-duration dual-purpose cowpea (65-75 days) matures safely within the 10-year mean rainfall window of 1170.3 mm.
Landscape dry-season background vegetation cover (NDVI 0.35) benefits from cowpea post-harvest residue mulch.

benefits: Disrupts Cercospora leaf spot and root-knot nematode cycles on groundnut-tired plots
Provides 35-50 kg/ha biologically fixed nitrogen to nourish following Early Millet cereal
Early cowpea harvest (September) breaks the household hungry season gap
Diversified income stream from high-value sesame in Season 3
trade_offs: Requires field scouting for cowpea pod borer (Maruca vitrata) during flowering
Sesame requires careful harvesting to prevent seed shattering losses
Requires sourcing certified dual-purpose cowpea seed (e.g., Dania or Iron cultivars)
gaps: Local availability of certified cowpea inoculant in West Coast Region agricultural depots
Partial soil texture classification (silt percentage unextracted in pilot SoilGrids dataset)
risks_for_local_review: Consult the local Brikama agricultural extension agent regarding approved cowpea varieties for sandy loams.
Confirm market pricing for sesame with local commodity traders before Year 3 planting.

strategies.name: Option B: Resilient Low-Input Drought Buffer Rotation
strategies.why: Prioritizes drought resilience, input minimization, and livestock integration. Deep-rooted sorghum (Kinto) thrives in slightly acidic sandy soil (pH 5.3), followed by groundnut and a restorative cowpea fallow cover.

evidence.observation: Gentle terrain slope (0.8%) allows deep root anchoring with minimal surface runoff risk.
Historical dry spells >= 7 days average 0.4 events/season; sorghum's deep root architecture buffers against mid-season drought.
Subsoil moisture assimilation (0.227 m3/m3) is accessible to deep sorghum root systems.

benefits: Exceptional tolerance to irregular rainfall and July-August dry spells
Produces valuable stover biomass for dry-season cattle and small ruminant fodder
Lowest synthetic fertilizer and seed capital expenditure
Gradual organic matter rebuilding through deep root decomposition
trade_offs: Sorghum grain fetches a lower cash market price than confectionary groundnut
Requires vigilance against grain-eating birds (Quelea quelea) during milky dough stage
Longer maturity duration (105-115 days) than Early Millet
gaps: SMAP moisture observations are mid-month snapshots rather than continuous daily averages
Exact subsoil compaction depth at the specific farm site is unmeasured
risks_for_local_review: Confirm family or community labour availability for bird scaring during sorghum heading.
Verify local livestock grazing agreements regarding stover retention on the plot.

strategies.name: Current Practice (Baseline)
strategies.why: Represents the farmer's established field practice. Provides staple food security and cash crop income, but carries elevated pest risks if legume-cereal breaks are omitted.

evidence.observation: July-Sept dry spells average 2.9 days. Fits current crop moisture demands.
Topsoil pH 5.3 is well tolerated by groundnut and pearl millet.
Farmer observed: "Sandy loam soil, observed early dry spell in July."

benefits: Familiar field management routine requiring no new seed sourcing
Reliable baseline staple cereal supply in cereal rotation years
Known market outlets for harvested produce in Brikama
trade_offs: Elevated risk of Cercospora leaf spot and soil-borne fungal pathogens if groundnut is repeated
Nutrient mining of soil organic carbon and micro-nutrients without green manure
High peak labor bottleneck during October lifting and stripping
gaps: No laboratory soil test for available phosphorus or potassium
SMAP soil moisture data is regional (~9 km grid) rather than field-probe specific
risks_for_local_review: Inspect field for early leaf spot lesions and parasitic Striga seedbanks before next planting.
Confirm that harvested seed pods are dried promptly to prevent aflatoxin contamination.

farming_system.farmer_observations: Sandy loam soil, observed early dry spell in July.

disclaimer: Decision-support suggestions only. Recommendations are grounded in historical NASA environmental reanalysis and SoilGrids spatial models. They do not constitute guaranteed agricultural outcomes or warranted yield predictions. Farmers and agricultural extension officers must inspect local field drainage, weed pressure, and seed vigor before field implementation.
